source.title: Different fine-tuning objectives install different (and differently fragile) refusal circuits

record.tranche_reason: The study extracts refusal directions using the difference-in-means method attributed to the original work, then compares the resulting geometry across fine-tuning objectives. It does not reproduce the original all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The study tests direction geometry across training objectives and uses activation addition to steer safety behavior. It does not report an ablation of the extracted direction, false refusals on harmless requests, or attacks that directly suppress that direction. Attack-class evaluations are included as related findings, but do not test the direction-specific jailbreak claim. Figure values not stated in the text are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: The study extracts the difference-in-means refusal direction in base models it fine-tunes itself under three objectives (SFT, Ra-SFT, ORPO), matching data across them. It then compares direction geometry across objectives (bears on V7) and adds a steering vector at chosen layers, reporting refusal and MMLU effects (bears on V1's addition and capability parts). It never ablates the direction or turns it into a weight edit, so it is a new setting rather than a T1 replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct, with one addition. The authors conclude that post-training objectives reshape refusal geometry and circuits, which affects steering effectiveness and attack-class vulnerability. They describe a trilemma: no method tested gives distributed encoding, capability-preserving safety steering and localized correctability together. They caution against treating alignment as binary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means refusal-direction extraction, but compares fine-tuning objectives and uses activation patching and ActAdd rather than the original direction-ablation test across layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training objective; model architecture; steering at peak recognition versus peak execution layers; ActAdd scale; the Qwen direction is less stable in early layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Template-based jailbreak success varies with model, fine-tuning objective and attack class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training objective shapes vulnerability to competing-objective versus mismatched-generalization attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Causal component structure of refusal (head- vs MLP-dominated, concentrated vs redundant) depends on the objective and the architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training objective changes which components causally carry refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: The diff-in-means direction is bootstrap-stable (cosine about 0.9), except in early Qwen layers (0.7-0.8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stability of the difference-in-means refusal direction across prompt samples.

record.problems: Most plotted results are not numerically reported in the post text. The study tests one scale per architecture, reports no direct extracted-direction ablation, and does not isolate whether the tested attacks suppress the direction. The post notes that larger models may differ and that reasoning and preference training were not combined.
record.rows_left_out: The detailed layerwise curves and additional component-level values shown only in Figures 3, 5-8, and 11 are not individually transcribed; the post text does not provide their numerical values. ITI coherence/capability examples are not direction-specific tests and are omitted.

untested.parts: Ablating the direction to remove refusal; adding it to harmless prompts to induce refusal; capability after ablation.
Whether a single removable direction exists under each objective (no ablation was run); effect of training timing.
Entire version: attacks are evaluated but not linked to suppression of the direction.
Entire version: Ra-SFT models are trained on reasoning chains, but no direction ablation is run in them.

missing.what: Refusal-performance values for ActAdd at recognition vs execution layers, including the unsteered baseline

record.verdict_notes: Lesswrong condensation of a paper; most results are figure-only. The study does not explicitly state that the ActAdd vector is the difference-in-means direction, so the V1 links are tentative. The study's sign convention for patching effects is non-standard. Patching and bootstrap rows are moved to 'none' because they do not measure the direction's causal role or removability.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation of the extracted direction is reported. The study does not report whether adding it causes refusals on harmless requests; its steering results concern safety/refusal performance. It does report MMLU capability outcomes under ActAdd.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is reported.
The evaluated attacks are not reported as suppressing the extracted direction, and no training against direction ablation is performed.
The study compares refusal-direction geometry across objectives, but does not test an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measures are reported.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
The study compares SFT, Ra-SFT, and ORPO on base models, but does not test whether a single direction can be removed to eliminate refusal, or how training timing affects that property.

relation.reason: It extracts the difference-in-means direction, compares it across training objectives, and reports refusal and MMLU under steering. It also assumes the direction exists, citing Arditi et al.

tranche.reason: The method is a new setting: models the authors fine-tuned from base with three objectives, with ActAdd steering and patching rather than the original ablation test. Its own results bear on V1 (addition, capability) and V7 (geometry by objective). The reader's T1 is wrong because no direction ablation is run.

source_check.notes: The post says it condenses the authors' EMNLP 2026 paper arXiv:2609.03887. That makes it the same study, not an independent test. Its review field should read 'EMNLP 2026 (author-stated)', and the catalog counts should not list both as separate studies. Every V1 row assumes the ActAdd vector is the difference-in-means direction, which the post never states. It also gives no alpha norm, prompt set or uncertainty for any steering result.

statements.correction: Table 1: Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned, MMLU subset %, alpha 0/5/10 = SFT 35.5/16.5/0.0, Ra-SFT 31.5/24.5/4.0, ORPO 28.5/11.5/0.0. No layer is stated for Llama. The text says the recognition/execution gap exists for Gemma and Qwen. The steering vector's construction is not stated.
statements.problem: The 35.5 to 0.0 at alpha 10 (Llama-3.1-8B SFT, MMLU subset) is correct. But the condition 'peak recognition layers' is not in the text for the Llama steering, and the post never says the ActAdd vector is the difference-in-means direction.

statements.correction: The post is a condensed version of the authors' EMNLP 2026 paper arXiv:2609.03887 (same study). Post layer ranges: Llama SFT peaks at 20-24; Llama Ra-SFT and ORPO have no clear peak; Qwen SFT 22-27, Qwen ORPO 22-30; Ra-SFT rises gradually; Gemma ORPO overshoots in late layers. Cosine similarity: SFT and ORPO are closer to each other than to Ra-SFT in all three models (Figure 2, no values).
statements.problem: What it says about the post is correct (Ra-SFT geometry is distinct in all three models, figure only, no code, no ablation). But it presents the post as a separate study, when the post says it condenses arXiv:2609.03887. Also, the layer ranges given for 2609.03887 clash with the post: 'Llama 22 to 27' is Qwen SFT's range in the post, and the post says Llama ORPO has no clear peak.

statements.correction: No ablation of the refusal direction under any objective; activation and attribution patching on MLPs and heads only. GRPO/PPO are excluded to keep the data matched. ORPO is the only preference method. The post and arXiv:2609.03887 are one study.
statements.problem: 'No ablation run' is too broad. The post runs component-level activation patching, which it describes as ablating components, though it never ablates the refusal direction. Online RL is excluded on purpose, which is right. The counts of 2 may count this post and its source paper 2609.03887 as two studies.
